title: Topological boundary state counts without universal gravity claims

items.title: Finite fusion transfer count model
items.statement: A **finite fusion transfer count model** consists of a finite nonempty label set $I$, a distinguished label $0\in I$, and an explicitly supplied matrix $N=(N_{ab})_{a,b\in I}$ whose entries lie in $\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$. The entry $N_{ab}$ is the multiplicity of elementary transitions from label $b$ to label $a$; formally, the transition copies from $b$ to $a$ are the triples $(b,a,j)$ with integer $1\leq j\leq N_{ab}$. A length-$n$ path is a sequence of $n+1$ labels together with a chosen transition copy between each consecutive pair. View each natural-number entry as a real number under the usual inclusion $\mathbb N\subset\mathbb R$. For a finite set $J$ and $F=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, $F^J$ means the functions $J\to F$, with pointwise addition $(x+y)_j=x_j+y_j$ and scalar multiplication $(\lambda x)_j=\lambda x_j$. For real matrices $A,B$ indexed by $I$, define $(A+B)_{ab}:=A_{ab}+B_{ab}$. Their action on $x\in\mathbb R^I$ is $(Ax)_a:=\sum_{b\in I}A_{ab}x_b$. Matrix multiplication is $(AB)_{ac}:=\sum_{b\in I}A_{ab}B_{bc}$; it is associative by regrouping finite sums. These definitions are compatible because $((AB)x)_a=\sum_{b,c\in I}A_{ab}B_{bc}x_c=\sum_{b\in I}A_{ab}(Bx)_b=(A(Bx))_a$, and $((A+B)C)_{ac}=\sum_b(A_{ab}+B_{ab})C_{bc}=(AC)_{ac}+(BC)_{ac}$. Thus the natural-entry powers can also act on real vectors and the addition used below distributes over matrix multiplication. Let $I_I$ be the identity matrix with entries $(I_I)_{ab}=1$ if $a=b$ and $0$ otherwise, and use the power convention $N^0:=I_I$ and $N^{n+1}:=NN^n$ for $n\geq0$. Define the vacuum-return count $D_n:=(N^n)_{00}$. If $D_n>0$, set $H_n:=\mathbb C^{D_n}$, with coordinates $x=(x_1,\ldots,x_{D_n})$ and inner product $\langle x,y\rangle:=\sum_{j=1}^{D_n}x_j\overline{y_j}$, linear in the first argument. This pairing satisfies the inner-product axioms of [[def-inner-product-space]]: finite distributivity gives $\langle\alpha x+\beta z,y\rangle=\alpha\langle x,y\rangle+\beta\langle z,y\rangle$, and conjugating the finite sum gives $\overline{\langle y,x\rangle}=\sum_j\overline{y_j}x_j=\langle x,y\rangle$. Writing $x_j=a_j+ib_j$ with real $a_j,b_j$ gives $\langle x,x\rangle=\sum_j(a_j^2+b_j^2)\geq0$; if this sum is zero, each nonnegative summand is zero, hence every $a_j=b_j=0$ and $x=0$. Conversely $x=0$ gives zero. The conjugation identities used here follow directly from $\overline{a+ib}=a-ib$ and finite distributivity. Therefore $H_n$ is a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space; its coordinate unit vectors form a basis since every $x$ equals their linear combination with coefficients $x_j$, and a zero combination forces every coefficient to vanish. Let $I_{H_n}$ be its identity endomorphism and define $\rho_n:=D_n^{-1}I_{H_n}$. If $D_n=0$, no normalized operator $\rho_n$ is assigned. The matrix $N$ is model data; no fusion category, quantum group, or representation is presumed to realize it.

items.title: Fusion path recursion and entropy
items.statement: For a finite fusion transfer count model, let $e_0\in\mathbb R^I$ be the coordinate vector equal to $1$ at label $0$ and $0$ elsewhere, and define $v_n:=N^n e_0$. Then $v_0=e_0$, $v_{n+1}=Nv_n$, and the number of length-$n$ paths from $0$ to a label $a$ is $(v_n)_a=(N^n)_{a0}$. Whenever $D_n>0$, the operator $\rho_n=D_n^{-1}I_{\mathbb C^{D_n}}$ is a density matrix and has von Neumann entropy $s(\rho_n)=\log D_n$ in nats. For the supplied two-label matrix $N=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$, with labels ordered $0,1$, one has $D_0=1$, $D_1=0$, $D_2=1$, and $D_{n+2}=D_{n+1}+D_n$ for every $n\geq0$.

items.title: Finite Hilbert boundary representation of Temperley-Lieb
items.statement:
Fix an integer $n\geq1$ and a real loop parameter $\delta$. Define $[0]_\delta=0$, $[1]_\delta=1$, and $[r+1]_\delta=\delta[r]_\delta-[r-1]_\delta$ for $r\geq1$. Assume $[k]_\delta\neq0$ for $2\leq k\leq n$; this list is empty when $n=1$. The abstract generator algebra $P_n(\mathbb C,\delta)$ is the unital complex algebra with generators $u_1,\ldots,u_{n-1}$ and relations $u_i^2=\delta u_i$, $u_i u_{i\pm1}u_i=u_i$, and $u_i u_j=u_j u_i$ when $|i-j|>1$. The diagram algebra $\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)$ has basis the noncrossing pairings of $n$ ordered bottom and $n$ ordered top points; its product stacks the left factor above the right, deletes each closed loop, and multiplies by $\delta$ per loop. Its elementary diagram $d_i$ has a cap joining top points $i,i+1$, a cup joining bottom points $i,i+1$, and vertical strands elsewhere. The isomorphism $\Phi_n:P_n(\mathbb C,\delta)\to\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)$ sends $u_i$ to $d_i$.

For every $1\leq i\leq n-2$, the adjacent relations in the presentation mean both $u_i u_{i+1}u_i=u_i$ and $u_{i+1}u_i u_{i+1}=u_{i+1}$. For matching the imported recursion's notation, write $U_i:=d_i$.

Set $p_1=1_1$. For $1\leq r<n$, put $Q_r=p_r\otimes1_1$ by adjoining one rightmost vertical strand and define

$$p_{r+1}:=Q_r-\frac{[r]_\delta}{[r+1]_\delta}Q_r d_r Q_r.$$

The denominator hypotheses make this recursion defined. For each $1\leq r\leq n$, let $\widehat p_r:=\Phi_r^{-1}(p_r)$. The cited Jones-Wenzl result gives $p_n^2=p_n$ under these unit-denominator hypotheses. For $1\leq r\leq n$, let $\iota_{r,n}:P_r(\mathbb C,\delta)\to P_n(\mathbb C,\delta)$ send each generator $u_i$ to the same-named generator, and let $\jmath_{r,n}:\mathrm{TL}_r(\mathbb C,\delta)\to\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)$ append $n-r$ rightmost vertical strands. The maps commute with $\Phi$: on each generator, both composites send $u_i$ to $d_i$ with those added strands, and both send the unit to the identity diagram. Since generators and unit generate $P_r$, the composites agree on every element.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space whose inner product is linear in its first argument and conjugate-linear in its second. A unital complex-algebra representation is a complex-linear map $\pi:P_n(\mathbb C,\delta)\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(H)$ such that $\pi(xy)=\pi(x)\pi(y)$ for all $x,y\in P_n(\mathbb C,\delta)$ and $\pi(1)=I_H$. Here $\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(H)$ is the algebra of complex-linear endomorphisms, with composition as multiplication and $I_H$ as unit. Require each generator image to be self-adjoint, meaning $\langle\pi(u_i)x,y\rangle=\langle x,\pi(u_i)y\rangle$ for all $x,y\in H$. Define $P:=\pi(\widehat p_n)$, define $\operatorname{rank}P:=\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{im}P$, and restrict to data with $\operatorname{rank}P>0$. The algebraic representation as a physical boundary state space is an additional model identification and is not part of this definition.

items.title: Jones-Wenzl image gives a finite maximally mixed sector
items.statement: Under the finite Hilbert representation data, let $r:=\operatorname{rank}P>0$ and $\rho:=P/r$. An **orthogonal projection** on $H$ means a complex-linear endomorphism $Q$ satisfying $Q^2=Q$ and $\langle Qx,y\rangle=\langle x,Qy\rangle$ for all $x,y\in H$. Then $P$ is an orthogonal projection, $\rho$ is a density matrix with eigenvalue $1/r$ of multiplicity $r$ and eigenvalue $0$ on $\ker P$, and its entropy is $s(\rho)=\log r$ in nats. Under the published closure convention, the unnormalized diagrammatic closure trace of the algebraic Jones-Wenzl element is $\operatorname{Tr}_n(p_n)=[n+1]_\delta$. The proposition records this separately from the ordinary Hilbert-space trace $\operatorname{tr}_H(P)=r$ and does not assert the two values agree. A sufficient additional hypothesis for equality on this element is that the representation preserve these traces, $\operatorname{tr}_H(\pi(\Phi_n^{-1}(X)))=\operatorname{Tr}_n(X)$ for every $X\in\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)$.

title: Topological boundary state counts without universal gravity claims — Examples

items.title: Fusion counts do not fix a gravitational area coefficient
items.statement: For the two-label matrix $N=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$ in the finite fusion count model, $D_4=2$. Choose a positive scalar $a$ independently of $N$, assign this same scalar to each of the four labels, and set $A_4:=4a$. The ratio between the model entropy $\log D_4$ and this separately assigned scalar is $\log2/(4a)$, and it changes when $a$ is replaced by $2a$ although $N$ and $D_4$ are unchanged. Thus the finite count alone does not determine a proportionality coefficient between its entropy and an independently assigned area-like scalar. The scalar $A_4$ is formal data in this mathematical example; no geometrical area, physical entropy, or gravitational law is asserted.
